6Eh8cU_rdGw.title: TEDAI Vienna Panel - Inside Intercom's Strategic Reinvention as an AI-First Company
6Eh8cU_rdGw.label: TEDAI Vienna 2025
6Eh8cU_rdGw.description:
In this intimate fireside chat about the future of SaaS in the age of A, Intercom Co-Founder of Intercom, Fin.ai Des Traynor shares why, and how, they rebuilt their entire product and business model around AI, and the existential implications for organisations hesitant to make similar transitions. This fireside chat is hosted by TEDAI Vienna Co-Organizer, Adverity Co-Founder and involve.me CEO Vlad Gozman.

N_kZ62-3MvU.title: TEDAI Vienna Panel - How do you lead as AI advances?
N_kZ62-3MvU.label: TEDAI Vienna 2025
N_kZ62-3MvU.description:
As AI advances and agents grow more independent, leaders face rising pressure to get it right. Autonomous AI-enabled organizations are becoming increasingly plausible, challenging traditional business models. Navigating these complexities of AI integration demands more than technical skill—it requires bold leadership, strong governance, and a steady human touch to manage risks, regulations, and workforce change.​ In this session, journalist Hilke Schellmann, Chief AI Officer at PwC Joe Atkinson, President and Group CEO of Cassava Technologies Hardy Pemhiwa, and Founder of AI Academy Asia Bolor-Erdene Battsengel discuss: How can human-centered governance act as a strategic accelerator for responsibly deploying autonomous AI at scale? ​And, how will it change the way we govern, whilst keeping pace with the tech? How can leaders balance innovation with control? How can leaders ensure human creativity and critical thinking remain central in decision-making processes?

Thumbnail © TEDAI Vienna | Robert Leslie

URLltASJKBI.title: TEDAI Vienna Panel - The Future Will Be Simulated: Inside the New Frontier of Industrial AI
URLltASJKBI.label: TEDAI Vienna 2025
URLltASJKBI.description:
What if the future of engineering isn’t about months of testing, but simulations that predict reality in real time? In this discussion, Co-Founder & Chief Scientist Johannes Brandstetter and VP People Carlota Alcázar reveal how Emmi AI fuses physics and AI to revolutionize industries ranging from aerospace to energy. Discover how they're building a European AI powerhouse at this interactive session hosted by TEDAI Ambassador, Perplexity Fellow, and N&P CEO George Nimeh.

Thumbnail © TEDAI Vienna | Robert Leslie

XK7A2z_lZKQ.title: TEDAI Vienna Panel - How to successfully roll out agentic frameworks across organisations
XK7A2z_lZKQ.label: TEDAI Vienna 2025
XK7A2z_lZKQ.description:
Autonomous AI is evolving from simply predicting outcomes to making independent decisions and taking actions on our behalf. In this context, we'll examine the rise of autonomous AI and systems like Agent OS to understand the opportunities they present for rapid advancement. Their effectiveness, however, depends on how well people can manage them. ​In this conversation, Chief AI Officer for PwC UK and EMEA AI Leader Bivek Sharma, journalist Jennifer Strong, co-founder of Intercom, fin.ai Des Traynor and researcher Mengchen Dong take a deep dive into these question: How will they define our roles as humans? How can you make agents your best performing assistants? And, moreover, as AI reshapes the way we work, what strategic investments in future ready skills are needed to complement autonomous systems?

Thumbnail © TEDAI Vienna | Robert Leslie

YBw7IrZBoAM.title: TEDAI Vienna Panel - Protecting human intent in a space of generative AI sameness & infinite outputs
YBw7IrZBoAM.label: TEDAI Vienna 2025
YBw7IrZBoAM.description:
As AI becomes deeply embedded in our creative and decision-making tools, it doesn’t just assist us: it starts to shape what we create, how we think, and even what we value. The promise of generative technology is abundance, but the hidden cost is often convergence / where outputs blur together, and intent is quietly overwritten by default suggestions. How do we prevent the erosion of originality and intention? In this conversation, Microsoft researcher Advait Sarkar unpacks how AI systems subtly influence our intentions and actions, from spreadsheets to copilots, and why friction might be essential to preserve critical thought. Designer and data storyteller Pau Garcia brings a cultural and emotional lens, showing how immersive, sensory storytelling can restore meaning, agency, and surprise in a world increasingly optimized for efficiency. Design is the only instrument we have for reclaiming agency in spaces dominated by automation. Guided by Ioana Teleanu, the three panelists explore what it means to treat AI as a design material - something we can mold intentionally, rather than passively consume - and how to design systems that resist homogenization, encourage human divergence, and protect the fragile spark of intent in an age of infinite outputs.

Thumbnail © TEDAI Vienna | Robert Leslie

eNQysSvBQgk.title: TEDAI Vienna Panel - What Actually Is the Good Life We Want to Create With AI?
eNQysSvBQgk.label: TEDAI Vienna 2025
eNQysSvBQgk.description:
Everywhere we look, we hear promises of “AI for Good” — and with it, visions of abundance and bliss. But what do those promises really mean? And what does the good life actually look like in an age shaped by Artificial Intelligence? In this conversation, tech philosopher Dr. Pia Lauritzen and Professor of Palliative Medicine Eva Katharina Masel come together to reflect on what gives life meaning, what fosters wellbeing, and how AI might help us get there. Hosted by TEDAI Curator Dr. Alina Nikolaou, this panel invites us to pause and reflect a future worth striving for.

Thumbnail © TEDAI Vienna | Robert Leslie
